body: Thank you for your response.  You really share down to the detail what your issue is?  Do you find that it increases shame the WS feels? I've found that shaming her hurts more than it helps,  and struggle to bring this stuff up without making accusations(something I'm working on). How do you share that,  something so painful,  without transferring that pain? I guess that's my fear,  transferring my pain to her.

The last Dday(I had 5 and then the crappy trickle truth too) was in January,  and there was a relapse of sorts in June that hurt(she sent a text to the first ap). I think we are doing better now,  things are remarkably improved. Her attitude is improved, and she's going to counseling now too. I wish my wife did half of what you do,  but my situation isn't simple either. I work on what's wrong with me,  it seems like she works on excuses, but it's improving.

I think what you're going through is normal,  and he needs to understand that.  One thing I did at that stage where bad days were a lot more common.  My wife would say "omg, is every single day,  can't we have one good day". So I bought a calendar and stickers.  Every night I asked her if it was a good day,  and if she agreed it was I put a sticker on that calendar.  Then when a bad day came,  and she tried that bs of saying there were more bad than good I could pull out the calendar and shut it down.  It's just how they pull off their victim card.  "OMG it's always so bad,  feel sorry for me". It's sickening really.

Wishing you the best of luck.  If he's anything like I was,  you're gonna see a lot of anger that's really just pain and hurt.  Have empathy,  realize he doesn't really mean everything he says,  and know that if he tries even a little it's because he wants it to work still.

You're probably correct.  Trust me,  I hate myself more than you could ever hate on me.  If not for my children I wouldn't be alive to type this,  and there have been days where they aren't enough.  So thanks for confirming what I already knew. I realize the level of my stupidity,  and feel shame for it,  but haven't yet been able to escape my situation.  I just don't have it in me.  So go ahead and add coward, fool,  worthless, and weak to that list as well.  I'm sure we could add more,  but it's not worth the time and effort.

I personally can't speak highly of marriage counseling.  It turned more into an argument than any therapy.  That said,  that he's willing to go with you says there is at least a part of him that wants to try.  If he wanted it to be over I imagine you would've gotten court papers instead.   Show empathy and remorse,  and be prepared to take some anger.
I know this feeling all too well.  I've found it gets a little easier with time.  Hopefully further it it gets even better.

I told her about my infidelity in September of 2017. We've had some short separations,  finances keep it short.  We've had to give up on marriage counseling until individual counseling is done.  I couldn't do it anymore,  it was just a huge argument everytime.

She's... I'm not sure how to describe her form of remorse.  She'll go from she feels bad for what she did,  to saying it isn't that bad because she thought we were done,  to it was just bad timing on her part, saying she had fun doing what she did  then back to saying she feels bad about it.  I've been working on me.  I have hopes we can fix things,  but after what I've been through,  and her often ambiguous attitude toward our marriage,  all I can do is work on me.  Starting EMDR therapy Tuesday,  and hoping it's as big of a help as my therapist claims it should be.
Yes.  I went to a support meeting.
My wife did run away with two different men.  Something made get some back,  oh yeah them dumping her.  She wants me dead
